title: Geo-smart retention and audit evidence playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a geo-aware retention policy and a repeatable audit-evidence collection workflow for Redwood Inference. It is intended for security, engineering, and compliance owners responsible for data lifecycle and regulatory evidence. The playbook aligns retention decisions, RBAC enforcement, audit logging collection, secure packaging of evidence, and exceptions handling into a single runnable procedure.

Scope
-----
- Applies to production and customer-managed private deployments (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers: API request logs, access-control events, key management events, tenant metadata, model artifacts used for inference, and audit traces associated with admin operations.
- Does NOT change application-level business retention for customer-submitted content; it augments platform retention and evidence mechanisms.

Definitions
-----------
- Evidence bundle: Time-bounded collection of audit/log files, signed manifest, and provenance metadata produced for an audit or legal request.
- Geo-smart retention: Retention windows and storage tiers that vary by data type and by geographic residency region (US, EU, APAC, CN where applicable).
- TTL policy: Enforced time-to-live configuration applied via retention controller.

Ownership and Roles
-------------------
- Security (owner): Priya Shah — policy steward and approver for retention tiers and evidence packaging format.
- Compliance (stakeholder): Aisha Khan — audit consumer and compliance sign-off.
- SRE (executor): Samuel Becker — implements retention controller and evidence export automation, monitors SLOs for audit retrieval.
- Product / Legal (request origin): Engages security for exceptions and legal holds.

Retention matrix (recommended)
-----------------------------
| Data class                         | US (default) | EU (GDPR) | APAC | Notes |
|-----------------------------------|--------------|-----------|------|-------|
| API request logs (metadata only)  | 1 year       | 6 months  | 1 year | Anonymize PII in EU unless opt-in |
| Auth and RBAC events               | 3 years      | 2 years  | 3 years | Critical for entitlement audits |
| Enrollment and identity proofs     | 7 years      | 7 years  | 7 years | KMS-backed, restricted access |
| Model artifacts (serving configs)  | 2 years      | 2 years  | 2 years | Store hash+manifest; artifacts may be ephemeral |
| KV cache content (prefixes)       | 30 days      | 30 days  | 30 days | Evict aggressively to reduce risk |
| Forensic evidence (legal hold)    | Hold until release | Hold until release | Hold until release | Legal hold supersedes TTL |

Retention rules: store logs encrypted at rest (AES-256), with KMS key per-region. Default retention is enforced by the retention-controller service and validated by daily audits.

RBAC and Enforcement
--------------------
- Principle: Least privilege with time-bound roles for evidence access.
- Role types: Audit-reader (read-only for evidence bundles), Incident-analyst (time-limited access with justification), Evidence-admin (can create/export bundles).
- Just-in-time (JIT) elevation is required for Incident-analyst via approval workflow in the access portal. Elevation must be logged and attached to the evidence manifest.

RBAC policy snippet (example)
---------------------------
- Policy name: evidence-exporter-policy
- Bindings: Audit-reader -> group:audit-team@example.com; Evidence-admin -> group:security-ops@example.com
- Constraints: evidence-admin requires MFA and a 2-hour session TTL.

Audit logging — required fields and retention
-------------------------------------------
Every audit event recorded in the platform MUST include the following fields: timestamp (RFC3339), actor_id, actor_type (service|user), operation, target_resource, request_id, outcome (success|failure), region, and correlation_id. Optional fields: raw_request, response_size_bytes.

Daily validation SLOs (examples)
- Audit log completeness check: 99.9% of requests must surface a request_id within 5 minutes of delivery.
- Evidence export availability: 99% of on-demand evidence bundles must be produced within 4 hours.

Evidence collection workflow (step-by-step)
-----------------------------------------
1) Triage and scope: Security/helper receives audit request (internal audit, regulator, legal) and records scope in ticketing system (JIRA). Attach date ranges, tenants, regions, and specific data classes.
2) Authorization check: Confirm requestor permissions and apply RBAC checks. If requestor lacks access, escalate to Evidence-admin for JIT approval.
3) Snapshot selection: Determine retention buckets and compute export windows. For large exports prefer time-window slicing (max 7-day slices).
4) Export command (example):
   - redwoodctl evidence export --tenant <TENANT_ID> --from 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-12-07T23:59:59Z --region eu-west-1 --output s3://evidence-staging/<REQ_ID>/
5) Packaging: Export produces raw logs + manifest.json. Build an evidence bundle:
   - manifest.json (signed by evidence-service key)
   - logs/*.ndjson (gzipped)
   - provenance.txt (human readable summary)
   - signature.sig (SHA256 over manifest, detached)
6) Hashing and signing: All files hashed with SHA-256. Manifest contains file digests and signing metadata (key-id, timestamp, signer).
7) Storage and retention labeling: Move bundle to compliant evidence storage tier (region-specific bucket with restricted ACL and separate KMS key). Label with TTL and legal hold flags.
8) Delivery and audit: Provide a secure presigned URL to the requestor; log delivery event with correlation_id. Update ticket with bundle checksum and storage path.

Evidence manifest example (text)
-------------------------------
{
  "request_id": "REQ-2026-12345",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-42",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "time_range": "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z/2026-12-07T23:59:59Z",
  "files": ["logs/2026-12-01.ndjson.gz"],
  "signer": "evidence-service@redwood-infer.local",
  "signature": "<detached-sig>"
}

Secure SDLC integration
-----------------------
- Retention and audit requirements must be captured in all PRDs touching logging, data storage, or customer data flows.
- CI test: retention-controller integration test must run in the release pipeline and verify TTL enforcement on a sandbox tenant.
- Pre-prod validation: Every release that modifies audit fields must include a migration plan and a backward-compatibility test that ensures older logs remain queryable for retention durations.

Incident response tie-ins
-------------------------
- If an incident demands enhanced evidence collection, the Incident Commander (IC) may widen collection windows and request immediate evidence export. The IC must update the incident timeline and record a temporary RBAC elevation for the export operator.
- For suspected exfiltration, preserve raw transport-layer logs and KMS access logs; mark evidence bundles as high-priority for preservation.

Exception and legal hold process
-------------------------------
1) Exception request: Submit the retention exception form with justification, data classes, regions, and proposed TTL.
2) Risk review: Security performs a risk assessment within 3 business days.
3) Approval gating: CISO (or delegated approver) approves/rejects. Approved exceptions are time-boxed and recorded in the Exceptions Register.
4) Legal holds: When legal hold is activated, retention-controller must set hold=true in the bundle metadata and suspend TTL expiry for affected objects. Legal hold overrides deletion and eviction rules.

Packaging and forensic best practices
-----------------------------------
- Evidence bundles must be immutable once signed. Store with object lock where supported.
- Maintain an evidence index (immutable ledger-style file) that records all exports: request_id, signer, hashes, storage path, and retention metadata.
- Where feasible, store a second copy in a separate cloud provider/region to reduce single-provider risk.

Operational playbook for auditors (quick run)
------------------------------------------
1) Validate scope and requestor identity.
2) Run export command examples (see workflow).
3) Verify manifest signatures and file hashes.
4) Confirm storage KMS key and ACLs; snapshot ACLs in evidence index.
5) Mark ticket as delivered and schedule a 30-day follow-up to confirm no additional requests.

Monitoring and validation
-------------------------
- Weekly automated tests: sample a set of tenant logs and verify TTL enforcement and manifest correctness.
- Monthly tabletop: run a dry-run evidence export for one tenant in each region and record time-to-complete. Target: under 4 hours for on-demand bundles.
- Alerting: Evidence-export-failure alerts to #security-ops with a P1 if exports fail for >6 hours.

Appendix A — CLI snippets and examples
-------------------------------------
- Export logs (small slice):
  redwoodctl evidence export --tenant tenant-42 --from 2027-01-10T00:00:00Z --to 2027-01-10T23:59:59Z --region us-east-1 --output s3://evidence-staging/REQ-999/
- Sign manifest (KMS-based):
  aws kms sign --key-id alias/evidence-service-key --message fileb://manifest.json --output-signature fileb://signature.sig
- Verify bundle hash locally:
  sha256sum -c manifest.hashes

Appendix B — Evidence packaging checklist
----------------------------------------
- [ ] Ticket with scope and approval exists.
- [ ] RBAC elevation logged (if used).
- [ ] Export completed and file-level hashes produced.
- [ ] Manifest signed and key ID recorded.
- [ ] Bundle stored in region-appropriate KMS-protected bucket.
- [ ] Delivery logged with checksum and proof of delivery.
